chapter_summary: Jesus rejects the claim that a man’s congenital blindness proves personal or parental sin, gives him sight, and meets him again after religious leaders question and exclude him. The man speaks for himself and grows in his understanding of Jesus.
main_lesson: Jesus reveals God’s work, hears an excluded man’s witness, and exposes confident refusal to see truth. Physical blindness must never be treated as moral or spiritual failure.

memory_verse.kjv: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
memory_verse.little_bible: He answered, “Whether he is a sinner or not, I do not know. One thing I know: I was blind, and now I see.”

parent_guide: Access: default for ages 6–8 and 9–12 with adult support. Ages 3–5 may receive only adult-led verses 1, 9, 12, 25, and 35–38; the full chapter is unavailable to ages 3–5. Sensitivity: congenital blindness, disability stigma, healing, Sabbath dispute, coercive questioning, exclusion, insults, sin language, and sight metaphors. Jesus rejects disability blame. Never teach that God caused disability merely to stage a lesson, that disabled people are incomplete, or that faith guarantees healing. The mud treatment is descriptive, not medical advice. “The Jews” here refers to particular leaders, not all Jewish people. Verses 31–33 record the man’s argument. Verses 39–41 use blindness metaphorically; never attach sin or ignorance to physical blindness. Some manuscripts at verse 35 read “Son of Man.”
application_for_children: Children may honour every person’s dignity, reject disability blame, listen when people speak for themselves, tell what they know, decline coercive questioning, and seek safe adult help with exclusion. Do not imitate the mud treatment or use blindness as an insult.

verses.kjv: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
verses.little_bible: As Jesus passed by, he saw a man who had been blind from birth.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus saw a man blind since birth.
verses.meaning: The verse describes congenital blindness without lowering the man’s dignity.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me notice people as people, not as problems.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus notice about the man without blaming him?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm that congenital blindness does not reduce anyone’s dignity or worth.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally write one respectful sentence describing the man without reducing him to blindness.

verses.kjv: And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?
verses.little_bible: His disciples asked him, “Teacher, who sinned, this man or his parents, so that he was born blind?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples asked whether the man or his parents had sinned so that he was born blind.
verses.meaning: They voice a harmful assumption that disability must punish particular sin.
verses.prayer: God, help me reject blame that treats disability as punishment.
verses.discussion_question: What harmful assumption did the disciples make?
verses.family_discussion: Name the false idea that disability proves someone sinned, and correct it together.
verses.do_it_today: Correct this myth aloud: disability is not proof of personal or family sin.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:2: The disciples quietly asking Jesus a question while the adult man remains present and dignified, no accusing gestures. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.
verses.little_bible: Jesus answered, “It was not because this man sinned or because his parents sinned. But the works of God were to be revealed in him.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus rejected blame and said God’s works would be shown in him.
verses.meaning: Jesus rejects both blame targets. This must not mean God caused disability merely to stage a lesson.
verses.prayer: God, may your work be honoured without shaming or using anyone.
verses.discussion_question: Whose sin does Jesus refuse to blame for the man’s blindness?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how God’s work can be welcomed without saying disability was caused for a display.
verses.do_it_today: Draw a dignity symbol beside the words “no blame.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:3: Jesus calmly answering the disciples beside the dignified man, warm daylight, no spectacle or cure-as-worth imagery. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
verses.little_bible: I must do the works of him who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus must do the Sender's works while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
verses.meaning: The image expresses urgency in Jesus’ mission, not compulsory productivity.
verses.prayer: Jesus, guide me in faithful work and needed rest.
verses.discussion_question: What do day and night picture in Jesus’ words?
verses.family_discussion: Compare the urgency of Jesus’ mission with the human need for rest; worth is not earned by productivity.
verses.do_it_today: Choose one useful task and one healthy time to rest.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:4: Jesus teaching about day and night to his disciples in a sunlit Jerusalem street, the man included without pity. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
verses.little_bible: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus is the light of the world while he is here.
verses.meaning: Light means Jesus’ revelation and life, not that sightedness equals goodness.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me welcome the truth and life you reveal.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus call himself?
verses.family_discussion: Explore light as a picture of Jesus’ revelation, never as a contrast that shames blind people.
verses.do_it_today: Make a paper sun labelled “Jesus, light of the world”; do not use darkness to represent disability.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:5: Jesus teaching in daylight with a small oil lamp motif, no darkness linked to disability. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,
verses.little_bible: After he said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and put the mud on the blind man’s eyes.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and put it on the man's eyes.
verses.meaning: This ancient action does not authorize unsafe touching or treatment.
verses.prayer: God, help me respect every person’s body and consent.
verses.discussion_question: Which difficult physical actions are described here?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that this is an ancient event, not medical advice; no one should copy it or touch another body without consent.
verses.do_it_today: No action needed; listen or pass. Never copy the saliva-and-mud treatment.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:6: Jesus kneeling to make mud on the ground beside the consenting adult man, action discreet, no saliva close-up. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.
verses.little_bible: He said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam”—which means “Sent.” So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus told him to wash in the pool of Siloam. He went, washed, and came back seeing.
verses.meaning: Siloam connects with Jesus’ being sent. The healing is not a universal guarantee.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me trust you without demanding a certain healing.
verses.discussion_question: What did Jesus tell the man to do, and what happened next?
verses.family_discussion: Order the events: Jesus speaks, the man goes, he washes, and he returns seeing. Healing is not guaranteed to everyone.
verses.do_it_today: Place three cards in order: go, wash, return.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:7: The adult man washing independently at the pool of Siloam, Jesus’ instruction recalled, no triumphant before-and-after comparison. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: The neighbours therefore, and they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?
verses.little_bible: The neighbours and those who had seen him when he was blind said, “Isn’t this the man who sat and begged?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Neighbours asked whether he was the man who begged.
verses.meaning: The question reflects uncertainty and social exclusion.
verses.prayer: God, help me see each neighbour’s full dignity.
verses.discussion_question: How had the neighbours known the man before?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss why a person should not be defined by disability, poverty, or a place where they sit.
verses.do_it_today: Replace a label about someone with their name or the word “person.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:8: Neighbours recognizing and questioning the dignified adult man in a village lane, no pointing or staring crowd. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he.
verses.little_bible: Some said, “This is he.” Others said, “He is like him.” But he said, “I am he.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People disagreed, but he said, “I am he.”
verses.meaning: The man speaks for himself while others debate him.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen when people speak for themselves.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important that the man speaks for himself?
verses.family_discussion: Practise pausing so a person can answer for themself instead of others deciding who they are.
verses.do_it_today: During one conversation, wait and let the person addressed answer first.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:9: The man upright and confident, speaking for himself while neighbours listen. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Therefore said they unto him, How were thine eyes opened?
verses.little_bible: So they said to him, “How were your eyes opened?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They asked how his eyes were opened.
verses.meaning: Questions should seek his account respectfully, not coerce him.
verses.prayer: God, teach me to ask kindly and accept when someone will not answer.
verses.discussion_question: How can a question be curious without becoming intrusive?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about respectful curiosity and a person’s right not to explain their body or health. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Practise saying, “You do not have to answer that.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:10: Two neighbours asking the man respectfully in an open public place, ample personal space. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.
verses.little_bible: He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, put it on my eyes, and said, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went and washed, and I received sight.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: He said Jesus put mud on his eyes and told him to wash in Siloam. He washed and received sight.
verses.meaning: The man accurately recounts events; the treatment is not to be copied.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me tell the truth about what I know.
verses.discussion_question: Which actions does the man say Jesus took?
verses.family_discussion: Notice how the man gives a clear account without the family imitating the treatment.
verses.do_it_today: List what the man says Jesus did, without trying any treatment.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:11: The man calmly recounting the sequence to attentive neighbours, Siloam visible in the distance. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said they unto him, Where is he? He said, I know not.
verses.little_bible: Then they said to him, “Where is he?” He said, “I do not know.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They asked where Jesus was. He did not know.
verses.meaning: Honest testimony can include uncertainty.
verses.prayer: God, give me honesty when I do not know an answer.
verses.discussion_question: What does the man honestly say he does not know?
verses.family_discussion: Celebrate that “I do not know” can be a truthful and wise answer.
verses.do_it_today: Use two columns: “I know” and “I do not know.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:12: The man answering honestly with an open hand while neighbours listen, no shame. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: They brought to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind.
verses.little_bible: They brought the man who had once been blind to the Pharisees.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They brought the man to the Pharisees.
verses.meaning: This begins an increasingly hostile religious examination.
verses.prayer: God, stay near people who are questioned or judged.
verses.discussion_question: Where do people bring the man next?
verses.family_discussion: Imagine how it may feel to be taken before authorities. Name a trusted safe adult who could help. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Point on a simple story map from the neighbourhood to the Pharisees.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:13: Companions bringing the dignified man before seated Pharisees, calm public setting, no threatening crowd. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.
verses.little_bible: It was the Sabbath day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus had healed him on the Sabbath.
verses.meaning: The Sabbath setting creates an internal Jewish legal dispute, not grounds for contempt.
verses.prayer: God, give us wisdom and mercy when we discuss sacred practices.
verses.discussion_question: What detail about the day begins the disagreement?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss the Sabbath disagreement respectfully without mocking Jewish practice.
verses.do_it_today: Listen to an adult explain Sabbath respectfully; no debate is required.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:14: A Sabbath setting in Jerusalem with Jesus, the man, and religious leaders shown respectfully, no anti-Jewish caricature. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Then again the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. He said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see.
verses.little_bible: Then the Pharisees also asked him again how he had received his sight. He said, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and now I see.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The man told them, “He put mud on my eyes. I washed, and now I see.”
verses.meaning: His concise factual account deserves listening rather than repeated pressure.
verses.prayer: God, help me speak clearly when others ask about my experience.
verses.discussion_question: How does the man answer the Pharisees’ repeated question?
verses.family_discussion: Compare this answer with verse 11 and practise listening without requiring unnecessary repetition.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally compare the man’s short answers in verses 11 and 15.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:15: The dignified man calmly giving a short answer to seated Pharisees, leaders listening, no interrogation pose. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keepeth not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them.
verses.little_bible: Some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath day.” Others said, “How can a man who is a sinner do such signs?” And they were divided.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some Pharisees said Jesus was not from God because he did not keep the Sabbath. Others asked how a sinner could do such signs.
verses.meaning: The narrative records disagreement about Sabbath and signs among Jewish leaders.
verses.prayer: God, give us humility when faithful people disagree.
verses.discussion_question: What reasons does each side give in the disagreement?
verses.family_discussion: Lay out both Sabbath arguments fairly; disagreement within Judaism is not a reason for contempt.
verses.do_it_today: Write each side’s reason on a separate card without choosing by mockery.

verses.kjv: They say unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, that he hath opened thine eyes? He said, He is a prophet.
verses.little_bible: They said again to the blind man, “What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?” He said, “He is a prophet.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They asked what the man thought about Jesus. He said, 'He is a prophet.'
verses.meaning: His understanding of Jesus develops through the chapter.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me grow in understanding and speak honestly.
verses.discussion_question: What does the man now say about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Trace the man’s descriptions of Jesus from “a man” to “a prophet.”
verses.do_it_today: Add “prophet” to a sequence of the man’s growing understanding.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:17: The man speaking confidently to questioners and calling Jesus a prophet, no submissive pose. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: But the Jews did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight.
verses.little_bible: But the Jews did not believe that he had been blind and had received his sight until they called the parents of the man who had received his sight.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Jews did not believe that he had been blind and received sight until they called his parents.
verses.meaning: Here “the Jews” means particular leaders, not Jewish people generally.
verses.prayer: God, protect people whose true words are doubted.
verses.discussion_question: What do the Jews doubt, and whom do they call?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss how disbelief can make someone feel erased. “The Jews” here means particular people in the story, not all Jewish people. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No action needed for this account of disbelief; listen or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:18: Questioners calling the man’s parents while he remains visible as an adult person, balanced power composition. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And they asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? how then doth he now see?
verses.little_bible: They asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? Then how does he now see?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They asked whether he was their son and how he now saw.
verses.meaning: The questioning treats their adult son’s identity and experience as evidence to check.
verses.prayer: God, help authorities ask questions fairly.
verses.discussion_question: Which two facts are the parents asked to confirm?
verses.family_discussion: Talk about asking for facts without treating a disabled adult as an object of investigation. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Sort the leaders’ questions into identity, history, and present sight.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:19: The parents facing formal questions with their adult son nearby, open space and calm expressions. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: His parents answered them and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:
verses.little_bible: His parents answered, “We know that this is our son and that he was born blind.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: His parents confirmed that he was their son and was born blind.
verses.meaning: They confirm facts they know without denying their son’s identity or dignity.
verses.prayer: God, help families affirm each person’s identity and dignity.
verses.discussion_question: What do the parents say they know?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm that the parents know and name their son’s identity and history.
verses.do_it_today: Write two facts the parents confidently confirm.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:20: The parents identifying their adult son with affection and dignity, no pity imagery. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: But by what means he now seeth, we know not; or who hath opened his eyes, we know not: he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself.
verses.little_bible: “But we do not know how he now sees, or who opened his eyes. He is old enough; ask him. He will speak for himself.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: His parents said they did not know how he now saw or who opened his eyes. They said he was old enough to speak for himself.
verses.meaning: Fear shapes their answer, while their words also affirm his ability to speak.
verses.prayer: God, help me respect another person’s voice and honest uncertainty.
verses.discussion_question: What do the parents not know, and who can speak for himself?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss both the parents’ uncertainty and their adult son’s right to speak for himself.
verses.do_it_today: Practise the safe boundary: “Please ask them directly.”
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:21: The parents gesturing toward their adult son as capable of speaking, leaders attentive, no infantilizing pose. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: These words spake his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
verses.little_bible: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed that anyone who confessed that he was the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: His parents feared exclusion for naming Jesus as the Christ.
verses.meaning: Religious exclusion can harm deeply; children should not be pressured to disclose belief when unsafe.
verses.prayer: God, be near people afraid of exclusion, and lead them to safe help.
verses.discussion_question: What fear shapes the parents’ words? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Name safe ways to seek help if a group threatens exclusion. No one needs to share a personal experience. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Choose a trusted safe adult or service you could contact about exclusion; no disclosure required.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:22: Concerned parents under pressure from community leaders, tension shown gently without threatening faces. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.
verses.little_bible: That is why his parents said, “He is old enough; ask him.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: So his parents told the leaders to ask him.
verses.meaning: The narrator explains their repeated answer without inviting shame.
verses.prayer: God, help me understand fear without shaming people.
verses.discussion_question: Why do the parents repeat that their son can answer?
verses.family_discussion: Consider the parents’ fear compassionately instead of calling them cowardly. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No action needed while considering the parents’ fear; listen or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:23: The parents repeating that their adult son can answer, family members shown respectfully. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Then again called they the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give God the praise: we know that this man is a sinner.
verses.little_bible: So they called the man who had been blind a second time and said, “Give God the praise. We know that this man is a sinner.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They ordered him to praise God and called Jesus a sinner.
verses.meaning: A formal demand for truth is paired with a prejudged conclusion and pressure.
verses.prayer: God, help me notice when religious words are used to pressure someone.
verses.discussion_question: How do the questioners combine praise-language with a fixed accusation?
verses.family_discussion: Identify how authority can sound religious while refusing to listen. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Circle the claim the leaders had already decided before hearing him.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:24: The man facing a second formal hearing, leaders speaking firmly but without looming or menace. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
verses.little_bible: He answered, “Whether he is a sinner or not, I do not know. One thing I know: I was blind, and now I see.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: He said, “I know I was blind, and now I see.”
verses.meaning: He separates what he cannot judge from what he knows by experience.
verses.prayer: God, help me distinguish what I know from what I do not know.
verses.discussion_question: What does the man know, and what does he say he does not know?
verses.family_discussion: Make room for a person to know one thing clearly without knowing everything.
verses.do_it_today: Make a two-item list: what he knows; what he does not claim to know.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:25: The man upright and composed, stating the one thing he knows, no cure-as-worth comparison. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Then said they to him again, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?
verses.little_bible: Then they said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”

verses.family_discussion: Agree on a family boundary: after someone answers or declines, repeated demands should stop. You may pass.

verses.family_discussion: Discuss a safe phrase for poor listening, such as “I have already answered.” You may pass.

verses.little_reader_adaptation: They insulted him and claimed to follow Moses.
verses.meaning: The conflict must not be used to belittle Moses or Jewish faith.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from insulting others or using faith as a weapon.
verses.discussion_question: How do the leaders misuse words and group loyalty? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Reject insults toward the man, Moses, Jewish people, or any religious group. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No action needed after the leaders’ insults; listen or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:28: Leaders speaking insulting words while the dignified man remains steady; Moses represented only by a respectful scroll motif. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: We know that God spake unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is.
verses.little_bible: “We know that God spoke to Moses. But as for this man, we do not know where he comes from.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They knew God spoke to Moses but denied knowing Jesus’ origin.
verses.meaning: John’s irony is that their claimed certainty does not produce recognition.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour Moses and seek truth about Jesus without contempt.
verses.discussion_question: What do the leaders claim to know about Moses and not know about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Honour Moses and the Jewish setting while noticing the leaders’ claimed uncertainty about Jesus.
verses.do_it_today: Place “Moses” and “Jesus” on a story timeline without ranking people by insults.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:29: Jewish leaders beside an honoured Torah scroll speaking about Moses and Jesus, historically respectful, no stereotypes. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: The man answered and said unto them, Why herein is a marvellous thing, that ye know not from whence he is, and yet he hath opened mine eyes.
verses.little_bible: The man answered them, “This is an amazing thing: you do not know where he comes from, and yet he opened my eyes.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The man wondered that they denied Jesus’ origin although Jesus opened his eyes.
verses.meaning: He points out a contradiction in their reasoning.
verses.prayer: God, help me notice evidence while remaining humble.
verses.discussion_question: What contradiction does the man point out?
verses.family_discussion: Follow the man’s reasoning from the opened eyes to his question about Jesus’ origin.
verses.do_it_today: Underline the two facts the man sets side by side.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:30: The dignified man calmly pointing out the contradiction in the leaders’ reasoning, open public room. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.
verses.little_bible: “We know that God does not listen to sinners, but if anyone worships God and does his will, God listens to that person.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The man argued that God listens to a worshipper who does his will.
verses.meaning: This is the man’s general argument, not a complete doctrine that God never hears a sinner’s prayer.
verses.prayer: God, help me read a person’s argument carefully and not turn it into a rule you did not give.
verses.discussion_question: Whose argument is this, and why should it not become a complete rule about prayer?
verses.family_discussion: Label verse 31 “the man’s argument” and avoid saying God never hears any sinner’s prayer.
verses.do_it_today: Write “speaker’s reasoning” beside verse 31.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:31: The man presenting his argument with one open hand, listeners thoughtful, no visual claim that disability equals sin. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind.
verses.little_bible: “Since the world began, no one has ever heard of anyone opening the eyes of a person born blind.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: He said such a healing had never been heard of.
verses.meaning: The claim emphasizes the unprecedented sign in his remembered history.
verses.prayer: God, let wonder lead me toward truth, not toward demands for miracles.
verses.discussion_question: Why does the man call this sign unheard-of?
verses.family_discussion: Discuss wonder at a unique sign without promising or demanding physical healing today.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally make a wonder mark beside the unprecedented claim; do not act out blindness.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:32: The man describing the unprecedented sign with quiet wonder, no before-and-after body comparison. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: If this man were not of God, he could do nothing.
verses.little_bible: “If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: He concluded that Jesus could do nothing if he were not from God.
verses.meaning: His conclusion advances his growing confession about Jesus.
verses.prayer: God, help me recognize what Jesus’ works reveal.
verses.discussion_question: What conclusion does the man reach about Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Trace the man’s conclusion while remembering that disabled people do not need a cure to have dignity.
verses.do_it_today: Draw an arrow from the sign to the man’s conclusion, without making healing a universal promise.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:33: The man concluding his reasoning about Jesus, upright and confident before seated leaders. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.
verses.little_bible: They answered him, 'You were completely born in sins, and are you teaching us?' Then they put him out.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They insulted the man and threw him out.
verses.meaning: The leaders repeat ableist blame and abuse authority; the narrative exposes rather than endorses it.
verses.prayer: God, stand with people who are insulted or excluded, and guide them to safe support.
verses.discussion_question: What misuse of power occurs here? You may pass.
verses.family_discussion: Name how insult and expulsion misuse authority, then identify safe help for exclusion. No personal story is required. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: No action needed; listen or pass. If exclusion worries you, choose a trusted safe adult.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:34: Religious authorities indicating expulsion from the gathering while the dignified adult man leaves upright; no physical throwing, violence, or threatening crowd. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
verses.little_bible: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out. When he found him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus found the excluded man and asked whether he believed in the Son of God.
verses.meaning: Jesus seeks him after exclusion. Some early manuscripts read “Son of Man.”
verses.prayer: Jesus, thank you for seeking the man after others put him out.
verses.discussion_question: What does Jesus do when he hears the man was put out?
verses.family_discussion: Notice that Jesus seeks the excluded man. Discuss safe, non-secret support for someone pushed out.
verses.do_it_today: Optionally send a kind, non-secret message to someone safely included in your life.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:35: Jesus finding the excluded man on a quiet Jerusalem path, warm welcome without pity. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?
verses.little_bible: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, so that I may believe in him?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The man asked who he was so he could believe.
verses.meaning: His question shows openness and incomplete knowledge, not forced certainty.
verses.prayer: Jesus, welcome my honest questions and give me freedom to learn.
verses.discussion_question: What does the man ask before believing?
verses.family_discussion: Welcome questions about Jesus without demanding an immediate answer or profession. You may pass.
verses.do_it_today: Write one honest question about Jesus; you may keep it private or pass.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:36: The man asking Jesus an honest question face to face, equal eye-level composition. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and he is the one speaking with you.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, “You have seen him. He is speaking with you.”
verses.meaning: Jesus identifies himself directly without devaluing blind people.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me hear how you make yourself known.
verses.discussion_question: How does Jesus identify himself to the man?
verses.family_discussion: Observe that Jesus speaks openly and directly; faith is not based on secret private instructions.
verses.do_it_today: Point to the words about seeing and speaking in the verse.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:37: Jesus speaking directly to the man in an open setting, both dignified, no secretive imagery. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.
verses.little_bible: He said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshipped him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The man believed and worshipped Jesus.
verses.meaning: His voluntary response completes his growing recognition of Jesus.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help belief and worship remain a willing response, never a forced one.
verses.discussion_question: How does the man choose to respond?
verses.family_discussion: Affirm that the man’s belief and worship are voluntary; no child must copy his response on command.
verses.do_it_today: Choose whether to sit quietly, pray, or pass; belief must not be performed for others.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:38: The man voluntarily worshipping Jesus while Jesus receives him; calm, non-coercive scene. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And Jesus said, For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see might see, and those who see might become blind.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, “I came for judgment: those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
verses.meaning: Seeing and blindness are metaphors here; physical blindness is not sin or spiritual failure.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me understand your metaphor without shaming physical blindness.
verses.discussion_question: Which words are literal and which use seeing as a metaphor?
verses.family_discussion: Explain that verses 39–41 use sight language metaphorically. Physical blindness never represents lesser worth or moral failure.
verses.do_it_today: Replace any phrase that uses blindness as an insult with respectful language.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:39: Jesus teaching a small group using balanced light imagery only as spiritual metaphor; no blind person, eyes, darkness, cane, or disability symbol. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: And some of the Pharisees which were with him heard these words, and said unto him, Are we blind also?
verses.little_bible: Some Pharisees who were with him heard these words and said, “Are we blind too?”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Pharisees asked whether Jesus meant they were blind.
verses.meaning: Their question recognizes that Jesus’ metaphor may challenge them.
verses.prayer: God, help me receive searching questions with humility.
verses.discussion_question: Why do the Pharisees wonder whether Jesus means them?
verses.family_discussion: Consider the Pharisees’ question without using blindness as an insult or game.
verses.do_it_today: Pause before insisting you are right and ask one honest question.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:40: Pharisees asking Jesus a searching question in respectful historical dress; no caricature or disability imagery. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.

verses.kjv: Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.”
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said, “If you were blind, you would have no sin. But because you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains.”
verses.meaning: The contrast concerns admitted need and proud claimed insight, not physical blindness or disabled people’s morality.
verses.prayer: Jesus, help me admit my need instead of claiming insight I do not have.
verses.discussion_question: What contrast does Jesus make between admitted need and claimed sight?
verses.family_discussion: Read both parts of Jesus’ contrast and keep the explanation separate from the metaphor.
verses.do_it_today: Use two cards: “admit need” and “claim to see”; do not act out physical blindness.
verses.illustration_prompt: Respectful storybook watercolour for John 9:41: Jesus answering the Pharisees with subtle open-and-closed scroll imagery for claimed understanding; no physical blindness imagery. Historically appropriate, disability-respectful, no caricature, no blank or clouded eyes, no text.
